narrative.location: GJ 667 C lies 23.63 light-years (7.244 pc) from the Sun.
narrative.host_star: GJ 667 C is a M1.5 V star with 0.33× the Sun's mass (effective temperature 3350 K, versus the Sun's 5772 K).
narrative.system: It is one of 3 stars in this system hosting 5 known planets.
narrative.planet: GJ 667 C f is 1.45× Earth's radius, at least 2.7× Earth's mass (a radial-velocity minimum mass, not the true mass), completing one orbit every 39 days at 0.156 AU, on a mildly eccentric orbit (e = 0.03).
narrative.climate: It receives about 0.56× the flux Earth gets from the Sun, for an equilibrium temperature near 220 K (Earth's is 254 K).

visualisation_disclaimer: Any rendering of this world is a scientifically informed visualisation, not an image. No exoplanet has been imaged at surface resolution. Surface and cloud appearance are illustrative of a physically plausible class, not observations.

mass_earth.class_meaning: Radial-velocity minimum mass: the true mass is M/sin(i), so this is a LOWER limit.

equilibrium_temperature_k.note: Equilibrium temperature excludes greenhouse warming by construction. Earth's is 254 K against a 288 K surface.

habitable_zone.model: Kopparapu et al. (2013), ApJ 765, 131, with the 2013 erratum coefficients

earth_similarity.caveat: A similarity metric on bulk properties. Not a probability of habitability, and not evidence of life. Venus scores 0.93 on the same metric.

evidence.source_coherence_note: NASA's composite row may select different publications for different parameters. Mixed-source is a disclosure, not an automatic quality penalty.

observability.reflected_light_assumptions: Geometric albedo 0.30, Lambert phase function at quadrature (1/pi). Scenario estimate only; not a measured contrast or detectability claim.
observability.tsm_note: Kempton et al. (2018) Transmission Spectroscopy Metric. Undefined for non-transiting planets.
observability.followup_note: Follow-up diagnostics are separate observing lanes and are not inputs to the default Earth-2.0 ranking.

transmission_spectrum.message: No published transmission spectrum exists for this planet in the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

transit_analysis.reason: Planet is not flagged as transiting; a light curve cannot show a transit.

rv_analysis.citation: This research has made use of the Data & Analysis Center for Exoplanets (DACE), operated by the University of Geneva. Buchschacher, N., Segransan, D., Udry, S., Diaz, R. (2015), ASP Conference Series 495, 7.

rv_analysis.instrument_offset_note: A per-instrument median was subtracted. Combining spectrographs -- or one spectrograph across a hardware intervention -- without this injects a step into the time series, which a periodogram converts into spurious long-period power.

activity_coincidences.interpretation: This RV period coincides with a periodicity in a stellar activity indicator measured from the same spectra. The signal is consistent with stellar activity and must not be treated as a planet without further argument.

keplerian_fit.caveat: THIS FIT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. The data cannot support an amplitude at this period; the value is reported only so the failure is visible.
keplerian_fit.msini_note: No mass is reported: the amplitude fit failed its reliability checks, so any mass derived from it would be meaningless.
